A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SD-RPN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, throughput measurements, component and training-data ablations, attention analysis and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds Qwen2.5-VL evaluations, threshold sensitivity results, resolution-scaling experiments, grounding comparisons and failure cases.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same sink-token removal, selective pseudo-label assignment, frozen-backbone RPN, BCE training and two-stage inference. Threshold retuning and additional backbone configurations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Table 11 adds an OCR-assisted TextVQA condition, whereas v1 explicitly evaluates without external OCR annotations. This adds a limited input-information scenario. Training datasets and benchmark domains otherwise remain unchanged; additional model configurations and DocVQA splits are protocol changes.

E2.justification: V3 retains S2 and ViCrop while substantially expanding comparisons. Table 2 adds Thyme and DeepEyes using published scores; Table 10 evaluates Grounding-DINO-B with one or two boxes; Table 11 adds reported comparisons with Monkey, LLaVA-NeXT, Mini-Gemini-HD and LLaVA-TokenPacker-HD.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adopts a background threshold of 0.05 instead of 0.10, although Section 4.1 still states 0.10. New protocols include Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B configurations, 576/up-to-4096 visual-token budgets, a resolution sweep, one/two-box grounding controls, OCR-assisted TextVQA and DocVQA test-split comparisons.

E4.justification: V3 adds foreground/background threshold sensitivity tests (Table 5), native-resolution versus SD-RPN throughput analysis (Figure 6), attention-noise examples (Figure 7), and explicit failure cases (Figure 9). Existing component, backbone-depth, data-size, RPN-depth and smoothing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained conditional-variance argument is theoretical reasoning, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise numerous SD-RPN scores: LLaVA-1.5-7B's document/OCR average changes from 34.3 to 34.6, V* from 67.5 to 70.7, and HR-Bench 4K from 48.0 to 47.3. Qwen results, threshold sweeps, timing comparisons and failure examples add substantial outcomes. Changed settings prevent treating all revisions as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The method equations and conditional-expectation, class-conditional-noise and variance arguments remain substantively identical. The theoretical discussion moves from Appendix E to Appendix F without new assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, two stated contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about annotation-free denoising and self-distillation, efficient RoI inference and data-efficient generalization. Additional model applications support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds explanations concerning feature reuse versus external grounders, attention noise from clutter and abstract queries, and dependence on base-model capability. Appendix E newly discusses incomplete activation, incorrect localization and spatial-reasoning failures, including cases where SD-RPN turns a correct baseline answer into an incorrect one.

D1.justification: V3 documents Qwen-specific attention and frozen-backbone layers in Table 7, visual-token budgets in Section 4.1, and Grounding-DINO box-selection rules in Table 10. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, training time, pseudocode, prompt templates and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix C substantially broadens positioning against external grounding and high-resolution/token-compression approaches, explaining claimed efficiency and data-efficiency advantages. Added references include Honeybee, TokenPacker, Mini-Gemini, Monkey, Thyme and training-free open-vocabulary segmentation; this extends beyond bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: V3 makes local wording edits, updates experimental descriptions and the publication header, adds acknowledgements, and inserts a comparison appendix with subsequent renumbering. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 expands Tables 1–2, adds Tables 5, 10 and 11, redraws Figure 1, and introduces success, resolution-throughput, attention-noise and failure displays in Figures 5, 6, 7 and 9. V1's qualitative Figure 5 is retained as Figure 8, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V1 left important questions about stronger dynamic-resolution models and alternatives to its RoI mechanism unresolved. V3's Qwen evaluations, resolution-scaling analysis and Grounding-DINO comparison substantially strengthen validation of applicability and efficiency. Concrete failure cases also qualify the method's benefits. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses introduced or left unresolved in v3, particularly inconsistent threshold descriptions and mixed OCRBench score scales in Table 11.
